Ryuichi Sakamoto | seeing sound, hearing time 2026.10.31–2027.03.14 Taipei Fine Arts Museum Galleries 1A, 1B https://www.tfam.museum/01skmt

The Taipei Fine Arts Museum (TFAM) presents “Ryuichi Sakamoto | seeing sound, hearing time,” the first major exhibition in Taipei devoted to the late composer, music producer, and artist Ryuichi Sakamoto (1952–2023).

The exhibition looks back on Sakamoto’s groundbreaking artistic practice from the 2000s onward. It features seven large-scale installations alongside selected archival materials from his 1999 opera LIFE , highlighting his long-term collaborations with five artists and art collectives: Shiro Takatani, Daito Manabe, Carsten Nicolai, Apichatpong Weerasethakul, and Zakkubalan.

Installation view of RYUICHI SAKAMOTO and SHIRO TAKATANI ’s LIFE–fluid, invisible, inaudible... , 2007, at “Ryuichi Sakamoto | seeing sound, hearing time,” Taipei Fine Arts Museum (TFAM), 2026 (left); and installation view of “Ryuichi Sakamoto | seeing sound, hearing time” LIFE Archive at TFAM, 2026 (right). Copyright 2026 KAB Inc. Courtesy TFAM.

By tracing Sakamoto’s reflections on time, life, the environment, and technology, the show reveals how he developed new forms of expression and sensory experiences of sound, opening up different ways for us to listen to and feel the world.

The exhibition invites viewers not only to view the artworks within a “space,” but also to engage with them through their own bodies and senses within a set “time.” Visitors can experience multiple layers of time—from the time of the work itself, to the time of their own experience and the time of the exhibition as a whole. Curated by Sachiko Namba, the exhibition encourages visitors to slow their pace and gain a fresh sense of how sound occupies space, how images trigger memory, and how the body experiences time in motion.
